The study was conducted using data from a 2.5 MW wind turbine and a 130 m meteorological tower at the Eolos Wind Energy Research Station in Rosemount, Minnesota.
The selected one-hour dataset had a mean hub-height wind speed of 7.8 m/s and a mean turbulence intensity ranging from 13% at the bottom tip to 5% at the top tip.
The normalized flapwise blade root bending moment varied from 0.7 to 1.0, while the normalized edgewise bending moment varied from -1.0 to 1.0.
The power spectra of the blade root bending moments showed distinct responses in three frequency ranges: lower (f < 0.01 Hz), intermediate (0.01 Hz < f < 0.08 Hz), and higher (f > 0.08 Hz).

In the higher frequency range, the flapwise bending moment spectrum had a dominant peak at the rotational frequency (0.22 Hz), while the foundation strain spectrum peaked at the blade passing frequency (0.66 Hz).
The leading-edge and trailing-edge strain spectra showed significantly lower slopes compared to the high-pressure and low-pressure side spectra in the lower and intermediate frequency ranges.

The magnitude of the high-pressure side strain power spectrum increased at outer radial positions, while the slopes of the high-pressure spectra in the intermediate range decreased, likely due to increased blade elasticity.
The low-pressure side strain power was highest at the 37.5% blade radius position, potentially due to differences in local flow separation along the blades.
The edgewise bending moment exhibited strong peaks at 0.97 Hz and 3.1 Hz, associated with the undamped natural frequency of the collective blade pitch control and its multiple.
The turbine power output was relatively insensitive to the change in turbine structural configurations compared to the blade root bending moments and foundation strains.
